reasoning_traces.think:
The core issue lies in extending simple S-R models to complex molar behaviors. The original theory assumes R emerges directly from S2, yet empirical reality shows that R depends on both S2 and environmental supports—discriminanda and manipulanda. These supports are not modeled in basic S-R frameworks, leading to a breakdown when applied to behaviors involving interaction with external environments. This implies that any formalism must include latent or contextual variables to represent supports. In GSI, this manifests as a Bayesian update where P(R|S2) becomes P(R|S2, supports), incorporating environmental context as evidence. In GSE, it translates into a transition system where T(S2, supports) → R defines valid state changes only when supports are present. The failure mode occurs when supports are ignored, causing misclassification or incorrect prediction of behavior. Thus, the mathematical structure must encode support dependencies explicitly through conditional probability or state transition functions.
